name: Elamipretide
status: FDA accelerated approval (Sept 2025) for Barth syndrome; other uses still in trials
mechanism: Binds cardiolipin, a lipid in the inner membrane of mitochondria, to steady the cell's energy-producing machinery

article.summary: Elamipretide (Forzinity) is a mitochondria-targeting peptide with FDA accelerated approval for Barth syndrome since 2025. Trials in other mitochondrial and eye diseases are mixed or ongoing.
article.takeaway: Elamipretide is a four-amino-acid peptide that binds cardiolipin, a lipid found mainly in the energy-making parts of cells called mitochondria. In September 2025 the FDA gave it accelerated approval for Barth syndrome, a rare genetic disorder, based on better knee muscle strength rather than proven clinical benefit.[^1][^2] The randomized part of the Barth trial missed its main goals, and a larger trial in primary mitochondrial myopathy was negative.[^3][^4] A phase 3 trial in dry macular degeneration is active.[^5] It is not a wellness or anti-aging product.
glance: Accelerated approval (Sept 2025) for Barth syndrome; a confirmatory trial is required[^1][^2]
Barth syndrome (approved); mitochondrial myopathy and dry AMD (studied, not approved)
Tiny Barth program (12 patients), a negative 218-person myopathy trial, and an active eye-disease phase 3

blocks.text: Mitochondria make most of a cell's energy. Their inner membrane contains cardiolipin, a lipid that helps keep the energy-producing protein complexes organized. In Barth syndrome, mutations in the tafazzin gene disrupt cardiolipin, leading to heart muscle disease, skeletal muscle weakness and low neutrophil counts.[^2]
Elamipretide binds to cardiolipin. It is thought to stabilize the respiratory complexes, improve the efficiency of energy production and reduce harmful reactive oxygen by-products.[^2]

The FDA granted accelerated approval to elamipretide (Forzinity) for Barth syndrome on September 19, 2025.[^2] The label covers adults and children weighing at least 30 kg, and continued approval may depend on a confirmatory trial.[^1]
Other uses remain investigational. A phase 3 study in dry age-related macular degeneration (ReNEW) is active but no longer recruiting.[^5]

rows: Neither main goal met in the placebo-controlled part; walking distance and symptoms improved during the open-label extension[^3]
No difference from placebo in the 6-minute walk or fatigue score at 24 weeks[^4]

blocks.text: The Barth approval rests on a very small study and on knee extensor strength, an intermediate measure. That is why the FDA requires confirmation.[^1]

items: **Most common:** injection-site reactions such as redness, pain and hardening[^1]
**Allergic reactions:** serious hypersensitivity, including rash and cough, has occurred, sometimes months after starting[^1]
**Benzyl alcohol:** the product contains it, so it is not approved for newborns[^1]
**Limited exposure:** the label's safety data come from 12 patients, some treated for up to 192 weeks[^1]

blocks.text: The company must complete a confirmatory trial for Barth syndrome. The dry macular degeneration phase 3 is the next major test, and a wider mitochondrial-disease program has had mixed results so far.

evidence.label: Moderate: approved on a small trial, mixed elsewhere
evidence.text: Approval for Barth syndrome rests on 12 patients and an intermediate endpoint.[^1] The largest randomized trial, in mitochondrial myopathy, was negative.[^4] Confidence will depend on the confirmatory and eye-disease trials.

faq.a: For one narrow use, yes. It received accelerated approval in September 2025 for Barth syndrome in people weighing at least 30 kg.[^1][^2] It is not approved for other conditions, aging or general energy.
A rare X-linked genetic disorder caused by tafazzin gene mutations that impair cardiolipin, causing heart muscle disease, muscle weakness and low neutrophil counts.[^2]

faq.q: Is it the same as MOTS-c or humanin?
faq.a: No. All three relate to mitochondria, but [MOTS-c](/peptides/mots-c) and [humanin](/peptides/humanin) are natural peptides encoded by mitochondrial DNA, while elamipretide is a synthetic peptide with a different target.
